key_insight: Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks can be used as physics-informed solvers for free-boundary PDEs by enforcing obstacle, complementarity, and boundary constraints directly in the loss.
engineering_relevance: This offers a flexible alternative to standard PINNs for engineering problems with contact zones or moving interfaces, such as phase change and obstacle-type mechanics.
method: Use KAN approximators inside a physics-informed residual loss.
Encode PDE inequalities, obstacle constraints, complementarity, and boundary conditions as penalties.
Test on linear obstacle, nonlinear p-Laplacian obstacle, and one-phase Stefan problems.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports numerical experiments showing low relative L2 and L-infinity errors and good recovery of contact regions and moving interfaces, compared with PINN and residual-network baselines.
watch_item: Performance may depend on careful loss balancing and interface resolution, which can be challenging in free-boundary problems.
paper_title: Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks for Free-Boundary Partial Differential Equations
